readability.summary: Each window as a client of its own is documented where it is decided and at each place it passes through. The host's documentation says how it tells windows apart by their channels, how it numbers them, under which client it keeps the panel layout of every window, and that a window that detaches shows nothing; the window's backend says why it opens one attachment per window, Theia running one backend for all of them. The switcher opens with how the foreground decides what the Explorer shows, what becomes of a folder that cannot be a workspace and of a window given several folders, what the title row names and when, and that each window is a client of its own; the title row's file names the workspace's place in the row. The conventions, the README, the manual and the architecture records say the same. Tests name the behaviour they prove. Review against the final code made the backend's header, its error at start and the README say that the backend serves the windows of the application that started it, no longer the one window; widened the tooling test that every icon is used to all of the window's TypeScript, now that the switcher uses icons too; gave the end-to-end check that no command adds a folder a control that the palette offers a command it has; and made the second window of the end-to-end test wait for its workbench before its Explorer is looked at, as every first window does. The host's tests of window numbers were made not to depend on which number a window gets, since the probe that checks a host answers takes a number for a moment. A reading of the evidence record against the code before the close made the check of the workspace opened from the list open it with a click on the workspace's name, as the manual tells the user to, with a seeded defect for it; made the state record and the conventions say that a window takes the lowest number free, not the n-th; made the manual and a comment of the switcher speak of the workspace a refused folder overlaps, not only of one that holds it; and wrapped one line of the backend's header to the width of the rest. The first logged end-to-end run found that TASK-009's check of the backend's refusal still looked for the old words of the error this task reworded; it now looks for the new ones.
